raw_response:
*Sitting down with a cup of tea to think about this year's plan*

Well, I've been working this land for forty years now, so I know what to expect from each plot. My 15 mu isn't much, but the soil on the east side is decent loam — that's where I keep my wheat-maize rotation going. The western 5 mu is sandier, so I keep that in cotton. It's been like this for most of the last decade and it works.

Here's how I'm thinking about each crop this year:

**Wheat (10 mu, the east field):** I'll plant in the second week of October, same as always. I use Jimai 22 — it's a good variety for our area, lodging-resistant, and I can save some seed from last year's harvest to cut costs, though I'll mix in some fresh seed every few years. Based on my yield last year (about 480 kg/mu) and the soil test the extension station did two years back, I'm planning around 17 kg N/mu, 7 kg P₂O₅/mu, and 5 kg K₂O/mu. I put most of the P and K down as compound fertilizer (45% 15-15-15) before planting, plus some urea as base. Then I topdress about 8 kg N/mu at jointing in early March when the wheat starts standing up. If the spring is dry I'll add a small topdress at heading too, but usually I don't. I'll irrigate 3 times — overwintering in late November, jointing in March, and grain-filling in May. Four waterings if it's a dry spring.

**Maize (10 mu, follows the wheat):** The tight turnaround is the hard part. Once I combine the wheat in mid-June I have maybe 3-5 days to get maize in. I hire the neighboring village's planter with the no-till direct seeder — costs about 25 yuan/mu but it saves two days and keeps soil moisture. Variety is Zhengdan 958 or whatever's fresh at the agri-supply shop. I apply a slow-release compound fertilizer at planting (one-shot, about 50 kg/mu of 28-6-8 — works out to roughly 14 kg N/mu), then if the plants look pale around V8 I'll topdress 5-6 kg N/mu of urea. No topdress if they look good. I usually irrigate once at tasseling if July rain is poor — last few years I only watered once or twice total.

**Cotton (5 mu, the sandy west field):** Plant mid-to-late April under plastic mulch — I've been doing mulch cotton for 20 years, it gets the soil warm and keeps weeds down. I buy hybrid seed each year, around 70 yuan/mu. Fertilizer is spread out: base dose of 40 kg compound at planting, then I side-dress urea at squaring (maybe 6-7 kg N/mu) and again at flowering (another 5 kg). Total nitrogen around 14 kg/mu. I irrigate 1-2 times during flowering-boll if it's dry. The hardest part is picking — with just my wife and me and me at 60, we can't do 5 mu of hand-picking alone. I'll hire seasonal workers from the village, about 15-20 worker-days over three picks in Sept-October. That's a big chunk of the cotton budget but there's no way around it.

**What I'm worried about this year:** Fertilizer prices are still higher than they were three years ago, but I'm not cutting back — I've learned the hard way that skimping on N at topdressing costs me 50-80 kg/mu of wheat, which is much worse than the fertilizer saved. My son works in Handan and sends some money, so cash isn't tight this year. Cotton price is what it is; I'll sell at the village collection point like always.
